name: BISAM
def: Mammal like four legged walking machine from Karlsruhe, built to study adaptive gait control with an articulated trunk.
body: BISAM followed the body plan of small mammals, with four legs and a jointed trunk that helped it shift weight while walking. Electric motors drove the joints and a layered controller combined reflex like reactions with higher level gait selection so the machine could cross uneven ground. It served as a testbed for biologically inspired control in the German legged locomotion community of the late 1990s.
facts: Used an actuated spine as well as four legs, unusual for the period
Part of the wave of biologically inspired walking machines built in Germany in the 1990s
specs: Layered reflex and gait selection controller
